title: Weeping Silver Lime: Ancient Weeping Limes You Can Visit
meta_description: A weeping lime that flickers silver in the wind: planted for a lost zoo in Ghent, beside a moat in Maastricht, on Alkmaar's old ramparts.
intro: A weeping silver lime is a grafted cultivar of Tilia tomentosa, its branches trained to arch back toward the ground, and every leaf carries a coat of white felt on its underside that flickers the whole crown pale in the wind. Three trees are mapped here, each planted by a park designer who wanted exactly that shimmer. Ghent's grew from an 1851 planting laid out for a private zoo whose grounds became Muinkpark once the animals left. Maastricht's stand in a group along the moated bank of Haet ende Nijt, planted in the 1860s to catch the light beside water, a generation before Lievin Rosseels redesigned that stretch of park around them. Alkmaar's is younger, from the 1930s, on the belt of old rampart earthworks the city turned into parkland. None of the three ages comes from a counted ring, only a register's decade band.
